metadata.title: zERC20 Privacy Token Protocol - Audit Map Batch 7

audit_items.title: Hash Chain Update Determinism and 248-bit Truncation

input_validation_bypass.findings: The _update function validates value <= type(uint248).max before updating. ShaHashChainLib.compute uses sha256 with abi.encodePacked which is deterministic for fixed-length types (uint256, address, address, uint256). No input validation bypass possible for the hash chain computation itself.

state_transition_violation.findings: Hash chain update occurs after super._update() succeeds, ensuring balance updates precede hash chain commitment. The index is incremented post-hash computation. State transition order is correct: balance update -> hash chain update -> event emission.

resource_exhaustion.findings: sha256 is a precompile with fixed gas cost. The computation is O(1) per transfer. No unbounded loops or dynamic memory allocation. Gas cost is deterministic and bounded.

faulty_error_handling.findings: ValueTooLarge error is thrown before any state changes if value > type(uint248).max. The super._update() call handles standard ERC20 errors (insufficient balance, etc.). No error handling gaps identified.

race_conditions.findings: All operations occur within a single transaction. Index increment uses post-increment ($.index++) ensuring atomic read-modify-write. No external calls between hash chain read and write. No reentrancy vectors in _update path.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted to construct scenario where hash chain could be non-deterministic: (1) Different transaction orderings produce same hash - impossible due to prev hash input dependency; (2) sha256 collision for different (from,to,value) tuples - computationally infeasible; (3) 248-bit truncation causing collision - requires 2^124 operations on average, beyond practical attack bounds.
phase_2_counterexample_construction.mathematical_bounds: 248-bit truncation provides 2^248 output space. Birthday bound for collision is 2^124 operations. At 10M tx/second, would take 10^30 years to reach birthday bound.

guards_found.description: value > type(uint248).max check ensures BN254 field compatibility

invariants_found.description: hashChain[n] = truncate248(sha256(hashChain[n-1] || from || to || value))
index increments by exactly 1 per transfer

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Guards and invariants fully cover the hash chain update mechanism

phase_4_classification.rationale: Hash chain computation is deterministic, correctly implemented, and protected by appropriate guards. The 248-bit truncation matches the BN254 scalar field requirements documented in the specification.

limiting_factors: Assumes sha256 precompile behaves correctly (reasonable assumption)

audit_items.title: IndexedTransfer Event Emission with Monotonic Index

input_validation_bypass.findings: Event parameters come directly from validated function arguments (from, to, value) and internal state ($.index). No user-controlled data can bypass validation to corrupt event data.

state_transition_violation.findings: Event emission occurs as the final operation in _update() after hash chain update. Index is post-incremented in the emit statement: emit IndexedTransfer($.index++, from, to, value). This ensures event index matches the transfer's position.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Event emission has fixed gas cost. LOG4 opcode cost is bounded. Index is uint256, overflow would require 2^256 transfers which is impossible.

faulty_error_handling.findings: Event emission cannot fail in Solidity. If _update reverts, no event is emitted. The atomic nature ensures consistency between state and events.

race_conditions.findings: Post-increment ($.index++) is atomic within EVM execution. No external calls can interleave between index read and write. Index is stored in contract storage, protected by transaction atomicity.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted scenarios: (1) Index skip - impossible, post-increment is atomic; (2) Duplicate index - impossible, each tx increments; (3) Event not matching actual transfer - impossible, same variables used for state and event; (4) Reentrancy causing index corruption - no external calls in _update path.

invariants_found.description: index[n] = index[n-1] + 1 for every transfer
IndexedTransfer event emitted for every successful transfer

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Event emission is guaranteed by Solidity semantics and EVM execution model

phase_4_classification.rationale: IndexedTransfer event emission is correctly implemented with monotonically increasing index. The event provides complete audit trail for off-chain indexers.

input_validation_bypass.findings: Transfer completion requires: (1) value <= type(uint248).max, (2) sufficient sender balance (handled by ERC20Upgradeable), (3) valid addresses. All validations occur before state changes.

state_transition_violation.findings: State transition sequence: validate -> update balances (super._update) -> update hash chain -> emit event. If any step fails, entire transaction reverts. No partial state updates possible.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Transfer is O(1) operation. Gas cost is bounded and predictable. No loops or recursive calls.

faulty_error_handling.findings: ValueTooLarge revert provides clear error. ERC20 errors (insufficient balance, zero address) are handled by parent contract. All error paths result in clean revert.

race_conditions.findings: Single transaction execution model prevents race conditions. No external calls in transfer path that could enable reentrancy.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted to find scenario where transfer completes but state is inconsistent: (1) Balance updated but hash chain not - impossible, same function; (2) Event emitted but balances not updated - impossible, super._update called first; (3) Partial revert - impossible, EVM provides all-or-nothing semantics.

invariants_found.description: sum(balances) == totalSupply
Transfer completion implies hash chain updated and event emitted

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Complete coverage through EVM semantics and explicit guards

phase_4_classification.rationale: Transfer completion is atomic and maintains all protocol invariants. The _update override correctly extends ERC20 semantics with hash chain commitment.

audit_items.title: Verifier Hash Chain Reservation Checkpoint Integrity

input_validation_bypass.findings: reserveHashChain() has no parameters - reads directly from zERC20 token contract. No user input to validate. Token address is set at initialization and immutable.

state_transition_violation.findings: Function reads (index, hashChain) from zERC20, stores in reservedHashChains mapping, updates latestReservedIndex, and emits event. State updates are atomic. However, there's no check preventing overwrite of existing reservation at same index.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Single external call to token contract, two storage writes, one event. Gas cost is bounded and predictable.

faulty_error_handling.findings: No explicit error handling for token contract call failure. If token() returns zero address or call fails, transaction reverts. This is appropriate behavior.

race_conditions.findings: IMPORTANT: Between calling reserveHashChain() and proveTransferRoot(), new transfers can occur on zERC20, advancing the hash chain. This is by design - the reservation creates a snapshot. However, if same index is reserved twice with different hash chains due to reorg, could cause issues.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: COUNTEREXAMPLE: If reserveHashChain() is called, then a chain reorganization occurs that changes the hash chain at that index, and reserveHashChain() is called again, the mapping would be overwritten. Subsequent proofs using the old hash chain value would fail NewHashChainMismatch check. This is actually a safety feature, not a vulnerability - prevents proofs against non-canonical chain state.
phase_2_counterexample_construction.severity_assessment: This behavior is intentional and provides security against chain reorganizations.

invariants_found.description: reservedHashChains[index] == hashChain at time of reservation
latestReservedIndex tracks most recent reservation

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Design allows overwriting which provides reorg protection

phase_4_classification.rationale: The reservation mechanism correctly creates snapshots for proof verification. The ability to overwrite reservations is a feature that protects against chain reorganizations.
code_quality_notes: Consider adding event for reservation overwrites to aid debugging

limiting_factors: Assumes zERC20 token contract returns accurate data

recommendations: Consider emitting different event when overwriting existing reservation for observability

audit_items.title: Nova IVC Proof Generation Requires Secret Ownership

input_validation_bypass.findings: Proof validation delegated to IRootDecider and IWithdrawDecider external contracts. The Verifier decodes proof parameters and passes to verifier contracts. No on-chain validation of cryptographic secrets - this is by design (ZK property).

state_transition_violation.findings: proveTransferRoot and teleport functions gate state changes on successful proof verification. State only updated after require(verifier.verify...) passes. Correct ordering of validation before state change.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Proof verification is delegated to external contracts. Gas cost depends on verifier implementation. Typical Groth16 verification ~200k gas, Nova verification varies. Bounded by external contract gas limits.

faulty_error_handling.findings: InvalidProof error thrown on verification failure. Emergency pause triggered on conflicting roots. Error handling is comprehensive.

race_conditions.findings: No external calls after state changes that could enable reentrancy. Proof verification is read-only from perspective of Verifier contract.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Nova IVC proof generation requires knowledge of secret inputs (private keys, note commitments). Without these secrets, generating valid proof is computationally infeasible under IVC soundness assumptions. Attempted to construct proof without secrets - would require breaking Nova cryptographic assumptions.
phase_2_counterexample_construction.cryptographic_assumptions: Security relies on Nova IVC soundness which depends on RLWE hardness assumption and Poseidon hash collision resistance.

invariants_found.description: Valid proof implies prover knows secret witness

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: On-chain guards delegate to external verifiers; security depends on verifier contract correctness

phase_4_classification.rationale: On-chain code correctly delegates to verifier contracts, but security ultimately depends on: (1) correctness of IRootDecider/IWithdrawDecider implementations, (2) soundness of Nova IVC construction, (3) correct circuit implementation. These are outside scope of this contract audit.

limiting_factors: External verifier contract implementations not audited in this scope
Cryptographic soundness assumed but not verified

recommendations: Ensure external verifier contracts (IRootDecider, IWithdrawDecider) have undergone cryptographic audit
Verify Nova circuit implementations match specification
Consider formal verification of circuit constraints

audit_items.title: Nova-to-Groth16 Conversion Preserves Semantics

input_validation_bypass.findings: singleTeleport() decodes Groth16 proof components (pA, pB, pC, pubSignals) and delegates to IWithdrawVerifier. Public signals are extracted and used for _teleport logic. No additional validation on proof structure beyond what verifier contract performs.

state_transition_violation.findings: Same _teleport() internal function used by both Nova and Groth16 paths. This ensures semantic equivalence for state transitions. State changes only occur after proof verification succeeds.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Groth16 verification is typically ~200k gas via precompile. Bounded and predictable gas cost.

faulty_error_handling.findings: InvalidProof error on verification failure. Standard error handling pattern.

race_conditions.findings: No race condition vectors. Proof verification is stateless external call.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Nova-to-Groth16 conversion (compression) is performed off-chain by the prover. The on-chain contract only verifies the final Groth16 proof. Semantic preservation depends on: (1) correct Nova circuit, (2) correct Groth16 circuit that verifies Nova proof, (3) correct trusted setup. Cannot construct counterexample without breaking cryptographic assumptions.

invariants_found.description: Groth16 proof valid implies original Nova computation was correct

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Security depends on trusted setup integrity and circuit correctness

phase_4_classification.rationale: On-chain verification correctly implemented, but semantic preservation depends on off-chain components: Nova-to-Groth16 compression circuit, trusted setup ceremony, verifier contract implementation.

limiting_factors: Compression circuit correctness not verified in this audit
External verifier contract not audited in this scope

recommendations: Document trusted setup ceremony process and participants
Verify compression circuit preserves Nova proof semantics

input_validation_bypass.findings: proveTransferRoot() validates: (1) proof passes IRootDecider verification, (2) oldRoot != 0, (3) oldRoot matches provedTransferRoots[oldIndex], (4) reservedHashChains[newIndex] exists and matches newHashChain. Comprehensive validation chain.

state_transition_violation.findings: Root storage only occurs after all validations pass. Conflicting root detection (existingRoot != 0 && existingRoot != newRoot) triggers emergency pause rather than overwrite. Correct precedence: validate -> detect conflict -> store.

resource_exhaustion.findings: External call to rootDecider, storage reads/writes. Bounded gas consumption. No unbounded loops.

faulty_error_handling.findings: Specific error types for each failure mode: InvalidProof, OldRootZero, OldRootMismatch, ReserveHashChainNotFound, NewHashChainMismatch. Emergency pause on conflicting roots rather than error. Well-designed error hierarchy.

race_conditions.findings: whenNotPaused modifier prevents execution during emergency. No reentrancy vectors - external call to verifier is first, then storage updates.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted to store invalid root: (1) Without valid proof - blocked by InvalidProof; (2) With mismatched old root - blocked by OldRootMismatch; (3) Without reservation - blocked by ReserveHashChainNotFound; (4) With wrong hash chain - blocked by NewHashChainMismatch. All attack paths blocked.

guards_found.description: Old root and hash chain consistency checks

invariants_found.description: provedTransferRoots[index] set only with valid proof linking to reservedHashChains[index]

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Comprehensive guards cover all attack vectors

phase_4_classification.rationale: Root verification and storage logic is correctly implemented with comprehensive validation. Emergency pause mechanism provides additional safety for conflicting roots.

audit_items.title: Withdrawal Proof Verification and Teleport Execution

input_validation_bypass.findings: teleport() validates: (1) proof passes IWithdrawDecider verification, (2) proof_[3] == 0 (initial last leaf index), (3) proof_[4] == 0 (initial total value), (4) proof_[5] == transferRoot, (5) proof_[6] == recipient. _teleport() further validates: root exists at hint, recipient hash matches, chain ID matches, value > currentTotal. Multi-layered validation.

state_transition_violation.findings: totalTeleported[recipient] only updated after all validations. IzERC20.teleport() called after state update. Correct CEI pattern: checks -> effects -> interactions.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Nova proof verification is expensive but bounded. Fixed number of storage operations. No loops.

faulty_error_handling.findings: Specific errors: InvalidProof, InvalidInitialLastLeafIndex, InvalidInitialTotalValue, FinalTransferRootMismatch, FinalRecipientMismatch, ExpectedRootZero, TransferRootMismatch, RecipientMismatch, InvalidRecipientChainId, NothingToWithdraw. Comprehensive error coverage.

race_conditions.findings: totalTeleported tracks per-recipient cumulative withdrawals. Multiple proofs for same recipient correctly handled - each adds to cumulative total. No race conditions due to monotonic increment pattern.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted double-spend: (1) Same proof twice - blocked by value <= currentTotal (NothingToWithdraw); (2) Different proof same recipient - only delta minted; (3) Wrong chain ID - blocked by InvalidRecipientChainId; (4) Fake recipient hash - blocked by RecipientMismatch. All double-spend vectors blocked by monotonic totalTeleported.

invariants_found.description: totalTeleported[recipient] monotonically increases
Minted amount = value - previousTotalTeleported

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Guards comprehensively prevent double-spend and cross-chain attacks

phase_4_classification.rationale: Withdrawal verification is correctly implemented with monotonic total tracking that prevents double-spend. Chain ID binding prevents cross-chain replay attacks.

input_validation_bypass.findings: validateFeeParams() checks: targetLiquidity <= MAX_TARGET_LIQUIDITY (uint128 max), k <= K_BPS_DENOM (10000), k * T * T fits in uint256. Raw functions also have internal overflow guards.

state_transition_violation.findings: Library functions are pure/view - no state modifications. Calculations are deterministic for given inputs.

resource_exhaustion.findings: All calculations are O(1) arithmetic operations. No loops or recursive calls. Gas cost is constant and low.

faulty_error_handling.findings: Overflow protection returns 0 rather than reverting in raw functions - this is safe because 0 reward/fee is conservative. validateFeeParams() reverts on invalid params during initialization.

race_conditions.findings: Pure functions with no state - race conditions not applicable.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted to find calculation errors: (1) Reward exceeds feeSurplus - capped by min(reward, feeSurplus); (2) Fee causes underflow - handled by liquidity >= fee check and clamp to 0; (3) Overflow in squaring - prevented by MAX_TARGET_LIQUIDITY = uint128 max; (4) Division by zero - T=0 returns 0 early. Edge cases handled.
phase_2_counterexample_construction.mathematical_verification: Verified formula: reward = k/(2T) * [(T-D)² - (T-U)²] matches documentation. Floor rounding for rewards (conservative), ceiling for fees (conservative).

guards_found.description: validateFeeParams checks target and k bounds

invariants_found.description: reward <= feeSurplus always
Reward uses floor rounding (never overpays)
Fee uses ceiling rounding (never undercharges)

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Mathematical calculations are protected against overflow and correctly rounded

phase_4_classification.rationale: IncentiveLib correctly implements the piecewise linear incentive curve with appropriate overflow protection and conservative rounding.
code_quality_notes: Excellent documentation of mathematical model in library header

input_validation_bypass.findings: computeAggregationRoot takes leaves and zeroHash arrays. Leaves come from storage (transferRoots), zeroHash precomputed at initialization. No external input validation needed.

state_transition_violation.findings: _computeBroadcastContext() creates snapshot of transferRoots before computing root. Root computation is pure - no state changes during calculation. aggSeq incremented only in broadcast() after root computation.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Tree computation: O(n) hashes where n = MAX_LEAVES (64). Each PoseidonT3.hash is ~25k gas. Max ~1.6M gas for full tree. Height padding: O(log n) additional hashes. Bounded and predictable.

faulty_error_handling.findings: Empty leaves array returns zeroHash[TREE_HEIGHT] - valid sentinel. No reverts in aggregation computation. Errors only for registration/broadcast constraints.

race_conditions.findings: Snapshot taken at start of broadcast - any concurrent root updates would be in next broadcast. aggSeq provides ordering. No race condition vectors.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted to cause incorrect aggregation: (1) Missing leaf - all registered leaves included in snapshot; (2) Incorrect zero padding - zeroHash precomputed from fixed formula; (3) Non-deterministic root - Poseidon is deterministic; (4) Height inconsistency - padding loop ensures consistent TREE_HEIGHT.

guards_found.description: MAX_LEAVES check prevents exceeding tree capacity

invariants_found.description: Aggregation root is Poseidon Merkle root of all transfer roots with zero padding
aggSeq monotonically increases

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Aggregation computation is deterministic and correctly padded

phase_4_classification.rationale: Hub correctly computes Poseidon aggregation root over transfer roots with appropriate zero padding to fixed tree height.

input_validation_bypass.findings: Hub._lzReceive validates: srcEid is registered (eidToPosition != 0), payload length == 64 bytes. Verifier._lzReceive validates: srcEid == hubEid. Source chain binding prevents spoofed messages.

state_transition_violation.findings: Hub only updates transferRoots if new index > current index (prevents replay). Verifier only saves globalTransferRoots if slot is empty (prevents overwrite). Correct monotonicity patterns.

resource_exhaustion.findings: broadcast() iterates over targetEids - bounded by registration. Quote functions called for each target. Fee refund loop - bounded by targetEids.length. No unbounded operations.

faulty_error_handling.findings: relayTransferRoot: NoProvedRoot if no root to relay, InsufficientMsgValue if underfunded. broadcast: EmptyTargetEids, NativeFeeMismatch, FeeRefundFailed. Comprehensive error handling.

race_conditions.findings: LayerZero guarantees message ordering per channel. latestRelayedIndex tracks last relayed. Out-of-order messages handled by index comparison. No race condition vulnerabilities.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted message spoofing: (1) Fake srcEid - blocked by eidToPosition/hubEid check; (2) Replay old message - blocked by index monotonicity; (3) Malformed payload - blocked by length check and ABI decode; (4) Cross-chain replay - blocked by chain-specific endpoint addresses.

invariants_found.description: Messages only accepted from registered/expected sources
Index-based replay protection prevents stale updates

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: LayerZero message handling is properly secured against spoofing and replay

phase_4_classification.rationale: LayerZero integration correctly validates message sources, prevents replay attacks, and maintains proper state synchronization.

input_validation_bypass.findings: GeneralRecipient struct contains chainId, recipient, tweak. hash() function computes sha256(chainId || recipient || tweak), masks to 248 bits, and encodes VERSION in high byte. No input validation - all values are valid.

state_transition_violation.findings: Library is pure - no state to violate. Hash computation is deterministic.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Single sha256 call (precompile) and bit operations. Constant gas cost.

faulty_error_handling.findings: No error conditions - all inputs produce valid output.

race_conditions.findings: Pure function - no race conditions possible.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted to find hash collision: (1) Different (chainId, recipient, tweak) producing same hash - requires sha256 collision (2^128 operations); (2) Version manipulation - VERSION embedded in result, cannot be changed by attacker. Stealth address derivation security depends on tweak secrecy, which is off-chain.

invariants_found.description: hash(gr) is deterministic for given gr
VERSION byte in position 248-255 allows future upgrades

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: On-chain component is correct; stealth security depends on off-chain key management

phase_4_classification.rationale: GeneralRecipientLib correctly implements recipient hashing with version encoding. Stealth address security is primarily an off-chain concern (tweak generation).

limiting_factors: Off-chain stealth address generation not audited

audit_items.title: PoseidonT3 Hash Function Usage and Correctness

input_validation_bypass.findings: _hashPair takes two uint256 values and passes to PoseidonT3.hash. No validation needed - all uint256 values are valid Poseidon inputs within BN254 scalar field (values >= p are reduced mod p).

state_transition_violation.findings: Pure function - no state transitions.

resource_exhaustion.findings: PoseidonT3 involves ~200 field multiplications. Gas cost ~25-30k per hash. Bounded and predictable.

faulty_error_handling.findings: Poseidon hash cannot fail for valid inputs. Library assumes correct PoseidonT3 implementation.

race_conditions.findings: Pure function - no race conditions.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Poseidon hash is a well-studied algebraic hash function. Collision resistance depends on MDS matrix and round constants. Cannot construct collision without breaking Poseidon's mathematical foundations.

invariants_found.description: PoseidonT3.hash(a, b) is deterministic
Collision resistance under random oracle model

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Security depends on PoseidonT3 library correctness

phase_4_classification.rationale: Usage of PoseidonT3 is correct, but the imported library implementation should be audited to ensure it matches the Poseidon specification.

limiting_factors: External PoseidonT3 library not audited in this scope
Round constants and MDS matrix correctness assumed

recommendations: Verify PoseidonT3 implementation matches specification (round constants, MDS matrix)
Ensure library is from trusted source (e.g., circomlibjs official)

input_validation_bypass.findings: validateFeeParams() validates: (1) targetLiquidity <= MAX_TARGET_LIQUIDITY (2^128-1), (2) k <= K_BPS_DENOM (10000 = 100%), (3) if targetLiquidity > 0, k * T * T must fit in uint256. setFeeParams requires FEE_MANAGER_ROLE.

state_transition_violation.findings: setFeeParams() validates before storing. Previous params discarded atomically. FeeParamsUpdated event emitted for observability.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Validation is O(1) arithmetic checks. No loops or external calls.

faulty_error_handling.findings: InvalidTarget and InvalidK errors clearly indicate validation failures. No silent failures.

race_conditions.findings: Storage write is atomic. Subsequent wrap/unwrap calls see new params immediately. No consistency issues.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted to set invalid params: (1) targetLiquidity > MAX_TARGET_LIQUIDITY - blocked by InvalidTarget; (2) k > 100% - blocked by InvalidK; (3) k causing overflow - blocked by maxK check; (4) Unauthorized update - blocked by FEE_MANAGER_ROLE.

invariants_found.description: feeParams always satisfy validation constraints

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Parameter validation is comprehensive

phase_4_classification.rationale: Fee parameter validation correctly prevents overflow and ensures reasonable bounds. Access control restricts updates to authorized roles.

audit_items.title: Stargate Bridge Integration Security

input_validation_bypass.findings: BridgeRequest validated: to != address(0), dstEid != 0. Amount validated through balance accounting. minAmountOut enforced by Stargate. Dust removal prevents Stargate InvalidAmount errors.

state_transition_violation.findings: Balance debits occur before Stargate call. If Stargate fails, transaction reverts. Fee refund logic handles overpayment. State is consistent before and after bridge.

resource_exhaustion.findings: External call to Stargate with bounded msg.value. Gas limit set by caller. No unbounded loops in Adaptor.

faulty_error_handling.findings: IMPORTANT: _unwrapAndBridge uses try/catch for quoteFee, unwrapSelf, bridgeUnderlyingTokenSelf, bridgeZerc20Self. Failures emit events but don't revert - this is intentional for lzCompose flow to avoid trapping cross-chain flows.

race_conditions.findings: Balance accounting per-user prevents cross-user interference. ReentrancyGuardTransient prevents reentrancy. SelfCall pattern prevents unauthorized internal calls.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted attacks: (1) Steal other user's balance - per-user accounting prevents; (2) Bridge without payment - balance debit before bridge; (3) Reentrancy via Stargate callback - ReentrancyGuardTransient; (4) Manipulate dust removal - uses Stargate's sharedDecimals, immutable.

invariants_found.description: User balance debited before any external interaction
Fee refunds credited back to user on overpayment

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Stargate integration is properly secured with balance accounting and slippage protection

phase_4_classification.rationale: Adaptor correctly integrates with Stargate, handling dust removal, slippage protection, and fee refunds. The non-reverting error handling in lzCompose is intentional.
code_quality_notes: Consider documenting the intentional non-revert behavior in lzCompose more explicitly

recommendations: Add explicit documentation for non-reverting behavior in lzCompose callbacks

audit_items.title: Nova IVC Folding Proof Chain Integrity

input_validation_bypass.findings: proveTransferRoot validates proof chain continuity: oldRoot must match provedTransferRoots[oldIndex], newHashChain must match reservedHashChains[newIndex]. This ensures each proof links to verified previous state.

state_transition_violation.findings: Proof chain: provedTransferRoots[0] = INITIAL_TRANSFER_ROOT (constant). Each subsequent proof must reference existing root. Chain cannot be broken without providing valid proof.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Single proof verification per call. No proof aggregation on-chain.

faulty_error_handling.findings: OldRootMismatch clearly indicates proof chain break. Emergency pause on conflicting roots protects against proof system failure.

race_conditions.findings: Multiple proofs can be submitted concurrently for different indices. Each targets specific (oldIndex, newIndex) pair. Conflicting proofs trigger emergency.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted to break proof chain: (1) Reference non-existent old root - OldRootMismatch; (2) Skip indices - each proof provides oldIndex, must match existing root; (3) Fork chain - conflicting roots trigger emergency pause. Proof chain integrity maintained.

invariants_found.description: Proof chain rooted at INITIAL_TRANSFER_ROOT
Each proved root has valid proof linking to previous root

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: Proof chain integrity fully protected by validation and conflict detection

phase_4_classification.rationale: Nova IVC folding proof chain correctly validated on-chain with proper continuity checks and conflict detection.

input_validation_bypass.findings: _onlySelfCall() requires BOTH msg.sender == address(this) AND selfCallEnabled flag in transient storage. Dual condition prevents: (1) external calls when disabled, (2) internal calls without enableSelfCall modifier.

state_transition_violation.findings: enableSelfCall modifier: sets flag true -> executes function -> sets flag false. Single-use pattern per external call. SelfCallAlreadyEnabled prevents nested enablement.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Transient storage (tstore/tload) is cheaper than regular storage. Constant gas overhead per call.

faulty_error_handling.findings: OnlySelfCall error if caller is not self. SelfCallNotAllowed if flag not set. SelfCallAlreadyEnabled if attempting double enable. Complete error coverage.

race_conditions.findings: Transient storage is transaction-scoped. Flag automatically cleared at transaction end even if not explicitly cleared (EIP-1153 semantics). No cross-transaction state.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted to bypass SelfCall: (1) Direct external call to onlySelfCall function - blocked by msg.sender != address(this); (2) Call when flag disabled - blocked by SelfCallNotAllowed; (3) Nested enable - blocked by SelfCallAlreadyEnabled; (4) Retain flag across transactions - impossible, transient storage.

invariants_found.description: onlySelfCall functions only callable via this.function() within enableSelfCall context
Flag always cleared after function execution or at transaction end

phase_3_guard_invariant_search.coverage_assessment: SelfCall pattern provides complete protection for internal callback functions

phase_4_classification.rationale: SelfCall pattern correctly implemented with dual-condition check and transient storage. Provides secure internal callback mechanism.
code_quality_notes: Elegant use of transient storage for transaction-scoped flags

input_validation_bypass.findings: LiquidityManager: IS_NATIVE_UNDERLYING flag set at construction. wrap() validates msg.value == amount for native. unwrap() checks address(this).balance >= amountOut. Adaptor receive() attributes msg.value to sender.

state_transition_violation.findings: Native wrap: msg.value added to balance before reward calculation uses pre-deposit liquidity. Native unwrap: balance checked before transfer. Order is correct.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Native transfers via call{value:}("") with success check. No unbounded loops. Gas for transfers bounded by 2300 stipend.

input_validation_bypass.findings: Admin functions protected by: onlyOwner (zERC20, Verifier, Hub, Adaptor), onlyRole(FEE_MANAGER_ROLE) (LM setFeeParams), onlyRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) (LM withdrawRewards, upgrade). All admin inputs validated (zero address checks, parameter bounds).

state_transition_violation.findings: Upgrades use UUPS pattern with _authorizeUpgrade requiring owner/admin. No time locks on upgrades - immediate effect. Critical operations (setVerifiers, setMinter) have immediate effect.

resource_exhaustion.findings: Admin functions have constant gas cost. No loops over user data.

faulty_error_handling.findings: ZeroAddress errors for invalid addresses. OpenZeppelin access control reverts for unauthorized calls. Consistent error patterns.

race_conditions.findings: Admin operations are atomic. No front-running concerns for owner-only functions (owner assumed trusted).

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted unauthorized access: (1) Call onlyOwner without ownership - reverted by OwnableUpgradeable; (2) Call onlyRole without role - reverted by AccessControlUpgradeable; (3) Upgrade without authorization - blocked by _authorizeUpgrade. Access control is sound.

input_validation_bypass.findings: lzCompose validates: (1) msg.sender == LZ_ENDPOINT (immutable), (2) _from == ZERC20_TOKEN (immutable). These prevent spoofed compose calls. Message decoding uses try/catch to handle malformed payloads gracefully.

state_transition_violation.findings: User balances credited (zerc20, native) before processing. Decode failure returns early (funds safe in balance). Processing via _unwrapAndBridge is non-reverting (try/catch pattern).

resource_exhaustion.findings: Compose callback gas limited by LayerZero executor. Internal operations bounded. No unbounded loops in compose handler.

faulty_error_handling.findings: CRITICAL DESIGN: lzCompose should not revert to avoid trapping cross-chain flows. Uses try/catch throughout, emits failure events (DecodeBridgeRequestFailed, UnwrapFailed, BridgeUnderlyingTokenFailed, BridgeZerc20Failed). User funds remain in balance on failure.

race_conditions.findings: nonReentrant modifier prevents reentrancy. Per-user balance accounting prevents cross-user interference. Compose calls are serialized by LayerZero.

phase_2_counterexample_construction.construction_details: Attempted attacks: (1) Spoof compose call - blocked by endpoint/token checks; (2) Steal funds via malformed message - funds credited to user first, decode failure is safe; (3) DOS via revert - compose doesn't revert, emits events; (4) Reentrancy - blocked by nonReentrant.
